info.title: Care+ API
info.description: Deterministic, synthetic active-ageing orchestration. Not a medical, diagnostic, emergency or surveillance system.

post.description:
Start one person's story over. `person_id` defaults to the demo person; any other
registered demo persona resets only that persona's run, and an unknown id is a 422.

get.description: The senior's own status, or that of the senior whose family group the caller is in.

schema.title: Response Person Metrics V1 People  Person Id  Metrics Get

get.description:
Who is signed in, which seniors they care for, and whether they still have to choose
`senior` or `family`.

post.description:
Choose once, right after signing up: `senior` (gets their own record, with synthetic
activity data until a real device is connected) or `family`.

A senior's 10-minute, single-use PIN. Giving it to a family member lets them link the
senior to their family group; asking again replaces the previous one.

Create a family group; the caller becomes its owner. With only `senior_name` the group
starts with no senior linked (`person_id` is null) until an active member enters the
senior's PIN (`link-senior`). With `senior_pin` the senior is linked at once and their own
account name is shown. A senior can only have one group.

Ask to join with a group's join PIN. The caller waits as `pending` until an active
member approves them.

get.description: The group and its members, including people waiting for approval. Active members only.

post.description:
Make this the caller's current group, as `last_opened` on `GET /v1/me` reports. Active
members only: anyone else, a senior included, gets 404, so `SignedIn` rather than
`Family`, whose 403 would answer a senior differently. Adds nothing to the family feed.

Link the senior to this group with the PIN on their screen; showing it is their
agreement. Active members only. Refused (409) when the group already has a senior or the
senior already has a group; a refusal leaves the PIN usable.

put.description:
Fix the senior's name while no senior is linked. Once linked the name comes from the
senior's own account (409). Active members only.

post.description: A new 7-day join PIN for this group, replacing the previous one. Active members only.
Let a pending member in. Any active member can approve.
Turn a pending request down. They can ask again with a valid join PIN.

get.description:
The senior's appointments (repeating ones as each day), the family's availability and
who is going along, from `from_date` to `to_date` (default: two months back, six ahead).

The family group's calendar, as the senior's calendar above, also before its senior is
linked (then `person_id` is null). Active members only; the senior reads their own.

post.description:
Fill in the appointment form from what the member typed. Saves nothing: the member
checks the form and adds it with `POST /appointments`. Written by the typed-appointment
agent when it is on and approved by a deterministic check, else by a plain parser. Active
members only.
Add an appointment, once or repeating. Any active member can.

put.description: Change an appointment (every day of it, if it repeats).

post.description: Remove an appointment (every day of it), with its answers and helpers.
Share a time you are free (or busy), whatever is on the calendar.
Take back one of your own shared times.
Available or not for one day of an appointment. Not available also steps you back.
Help with one day of an appointment (and so also be available for it).
Stop helping with one day of an appointment. Your availability answer is kept.

get.description:
What the family has done in the group, newest first. `before` is the `next_before` of
the previous page. Active members only; the senior never reads it.

"Since you last visited": what changed in the group after `since`, what still needs
someone, and today's tasks, written by the catch-up agent when it is on and approved by a
deterministic check, else assembled without a model. Reads only what the feed, calendar
and task list already show this member. Active members only; the senior never reads it.

post.description:
Tell the group you called, visited or messaged the senior, with an optional note for the
group. Nothing is sent to the senior.

Ask an active member, by name, to take one day of an appointment that needs a helper.
They get a notification. 422 for yourself, someone not active in the group, a current
helper, a day that has started or no longer needs a helper; 409 when someone has already
been asked for that day.

get.description: The group's open asks (asks whose day has started lapse first). Active members only.

post.description: The asked member says yes and becomes the helper for that day; the asker is told.
The asked member says no; the day needs a helper again and the asker is told.
The asker takes the ask back; the asked member is told.

get.description:
The caller's notifications across their family groups, newest first, with the unread
count. `before` is the `next_before` of the previous page. Never for the senior.

post.description: Mark your notifications read: the ones named, or `all`. Other ids are ignored.

get.description:
The family's notes on one day of an appointment, oldest first (at most 100). Active
members only; the senior never reads them.

schema.title: Response List Appointment Notes V1 Groups  Group Id  Appointments  Appointment Id  Notes Get

post.description:
Add a note to one day of an appointment, for the group only. The feed records that a
note was added, not what it said.
Remove one of your own notes. Its feed entry stays.

get.description:
The family group's tasks and the days ticked off from `from_date` to `to_date` (default:
two months back, six ahead), also before its senior is linked. Active members only.

post.description: Add a task, once or repeating. Any active member can; the senior cannot.

get.description:
The senior's tasks, as the group's above. The senior reads their own; a family member
the senior whose group they are an active member of.

"Read my day": a short script of today's appointments and reminders and tomorrow's
first appointment, for the browser to read aloud. Written by the "Read my day" agent when
it is on and approved by a deterministic check, else assembled without a model. Reads only
what the senior's calendar and task list already show; the same readers as those.

Whether "Read my day" can speak with the Kokoro voice here (it loads the model the first
time, so the first reading does not wait). The same readers as `my-day`.

post.description:
One sentence of "Read my day", spoken by the Kokoro voice on this server's CPU (no
cloud service). The same readers as `my-day`. 503 when Kokoro or its model files are not
installed, or it failed: the browser then reads with its own voice.

503.description: The Kokoro voice is not installed or could not speak.

put.description: Change a task (every day of it, if it repeats). Days already ticked off stay ticked.

post.description: Remove a task (every day of it) and its ticks.

put.description: Tick one day of a task done, or not done. Today or a past day; never a future one.
The senior ticks one of today's tasks done, or not done. Today only.

get.description:
The senior's watch: connected or not, last sync and battery, so the family can remind
them to charge it. Simulated until a real device is connected (`source` says so).

post.description:
One answer from the Care+ assistant. It only reads and explains: it never changes
anything. Emergencies and questions about medicines get a fixed answer.

AccountRole.title: AccountRole
AccountRole.description: What someone signs up as. Only these two roles can be chosen; the rest are provisioned.

event.title: Event
event.description: activity_declines, rain_explains_decline, rain_clears_activity_low, recovery, low_wear, consent_revoked, public_holiday, programme_becomes_full, or weather_turns

event_id.title: Event Id
event_id.description: Optional client idempotency key scoped to the active scenario run.

person_id.title: Person Id
person_id.description: Optional target person. Defaults to the demo person when omitted.

AgentStep.title: AgentStep
AgentStep.description: One step a family-facing agent took: a tool it read, or its submission and the verdict.

AppointmentDraft.title: AppointmentDraft
AppointmentDraft.description:
The appointment form, filled in from what was typed. Nothing is saved: the family member
checks the form and saves it with the ordinary `POST /appointments`.

Each field is null when it was not recognised; `missing` names those, `assumed` names the ones
filled in without being said (an end an hour after the start, a best-guess kind), and
`clashes` the titles of the group's appointments that overlap the slot. `mode`, `source`,
`model` and `steps` as on `CatchUp`; notes are never filled in.

AppointmentDraftRequest.title: AppointmentDraftRequest
AppointmentDraftRequest.description:
What a family member typed to describe an appointment ("Eye check-up next Tuesday 10:30 at
Bedok Polyclinic"). Never stored and never logged.

AppointmentNoteRequest.title: AppointmentNoteRequest
AppointmentNoteRequest.description:
A note on one day of an appointment, for the family group only: the senior never reads it,
and it is never logged, audited or given to the agent.

AppointmentOccurrence.title: AppointmentOccurrence
AppointmentOccurrence.description:
One day of an appointment. `occurrence_id` is `<appointment_id>@<YYYY-MM-DD>`: what
availability answers and helpers are attached to, so each week of a weekly visit has its own.

AppointmentRequest.title: AppointmentRequest
AppointmentRequest.description:
A new or changed appointment. A repeating one is stored once and shown on every day it
repeats, until `repeat_until` (inclusive) or forever.

AssistantChatRequest.title: AssistantChatRequest
AssistantChatRequest.description:
The conversation so far (the newest turn last, and it is theirs), which senior it is about,
and the page they are on. Only the last 20 turns are sent.

AssistantMessage.title: AssistantMessage
AssistantMessage.description: One turn of the chat, as the person saw it.

AssistantReply.title: AssistantReply
AssistantReply.description:
The assistant's answer. `source` says where it came from: `openai`, the built-in `helper`
(no AI key, the offline demo, or the AI could not be reached), or a fixed `safety` answer
(an emergency or a question about medicines, which never goes to the AI).

AvailabilityRequest.title: AvailabilityRequest
AvailabilityRequest.description: A window of time the caller is (or is not) free, whatever is on the calendar.

BaselineConfirmationQuestion.title: BaselineConfirmationQuestion
BaselineConfirmationQuestion.description:
Asked only when `analytics.BASELINE_DRIFT_FLOOR`'s clamp has been binding long enough that
it plausibly describes a permanent change rather than a passing decline -- see
`baseline_confirmation.py`. `question` is the exact plain-language wording shown; there is no
percentage, band or internal vocabulary in it, by the same rule every senior-facing surface in
this product follows.

`streak_days` and `asked_because` are never rendered -- they exist so the decision is
auditable as earned rather than merely asked.

CaseResolution.title: CaseResolution
CaseResolution.description:
Why a review case ended. Set once, at the moment it closes, and never inferred.

A case has exactly three endings and nothing else may close one: the person's activity came
back, they withdrew consent, or a coordinator answered the question the case was asking. The
reason used to live only in the prose of a `CaseReviewRow.note` written by `reviewer="system"`,
which meant anything wanting to act on it had to string-match an English sentence -- and a
coordinator reading the card saw "Resolved" with no reason attached at all.

CatchUp.title: CatchUp
CatchUp.description:
"Since you last visited": a short catch-up for a family member opening Home.

`mode` is `agent` when the catch-up agent wrote it and the deterministic check approved it;
any `fallback_*` mode means Care+ assembled the same facts without a model (the flag is off,
the provider failed, or nothing passed the check). `source` says which model wrote an `agent`
result: `live` (a real provider) or `recorded` (a replayed recording); it is null otherwise.
`steps` is what the agent did, in order.

CheckInRequest.title: CheckInRequest
CheckInRequest.description:
A family member telling the group they called, visited or messaged the senior. The note is
for the group only: it is never sent to the senior, the agent or the audit trail.

ContextAnswerValue.title: ContextAnswerValue
ContextAnswerValue.description:
The five answers the one question offers, and the only five it accepts.

The options are fixed server-side (`context_question._OPTIONS`); the senior surface renders
them as taps, never as a text box. `value` was nonetheless a bare `str`, so anything a client
sent -- a paragraph, an injected instruction -- was stored, echoed back and written into the
audit detail verbatim, and anything longer than the column became a 500 on PostgreSQL. Closed
here so the operator-readable audit trail can keep recording the token unredacted, which is
the whole reason it is exempt from the free-text redaction rule the `note` beside it obeys.

`PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY` is not a client-side dismissal: a question Care+ calls optional must
be answerable with "no", and recording that is what stops it being asked again.

ContextGapCategory.title: ContextGapCategory
ContextGapCategory.description:
What kind of known context explained a review, when a coordinator chose to say.

Optional, and allowed only beside an `OVERRIDE` for `KNOWN_CONTEXT`. It is tallied per person so
a care team can see which context Care+ keeps missing; it never changes a decision, a
proposal or a review setting. `ALREADY_IN_TOUCH` (in touch through another service or family)
is deliberately distinct from `OverrideReason.RECENT_CONTACT`, which is outreach the care team
already made.

ContextQuestion.title: ContextQuestion
ContextQuestion.description:
A single question, asked only when the missing fact would change what Care+ does.

The restraint is the feature. A question that does not change the outcome reads as scripted,
and a system that asks whenever it is uncertain becomes an interrogation -- which is exactly
what the people this is for have too much of already.

`asked_because` names the specific gap, so the question is auditable as decision-changing
rather than merely conversational.

CreateGroupRequest.title: CreateGroupRequest
CreateGroupRequest.description:
`senior_name` alone creates a group with no senior linked yet; `senior_pin` (the PIN on the
senior's screen) creates it linked, and the senior's own account name wins. At least one.

DeclineReason.title: DeclineReason
DeclineReason.description:
Optional, one-tap, always skippable context on a decline.

`ALREADY_ACTIVE` is the valuable one: it is a person telling us the sensor is wrong, which is
ground truth no wearable produces on its own and which feeds the data-quality assessment.

FamilyActivityEntry.title: FamilyActivityEntry
FamilyActivityEntry.description: One entry of the family feed: structured fields only, the browser writes the sentence.

FamilyActivityKind.title: FamilyActivityKind
FamilyActivityKind.description: What a feed entry records. Closed: the browser words each one itself.

FamilyActivityPage.title: FamilyActivityPage
FamilyActivityPage.description: Newest first. Pass `next_before` as `before` for the next page; None at the end.

HelperAskRequest.title: HelperAskRequest
HelperAskRequest.description: Ask an active member of the group to take one day of an appointment.

HelperAskState.title: HelperAskState
HelperAskState.description: An ask is `open` until it ends in exactly one of the other states; it never reopens.

HumanAction.title: HumanAction
HumanAction.description:
What the coordinator decided to do about Care+'s recommendation.

Three values, not a menu of care actions: the case card asks one question -- do you agree with
what this system suggested? -- and this answers it. `HOLD` is deliberately distinct from both:
"I am not acting on this yet" is neither agreement nor disagreement, and collapsing it into
either would overstate how often a human endorsed or overruled the system.

Nothing on the activity learning or ranking path reads this. One combination is read: a
resolved `OVERRIDE` with a false-alarm `OverrideReason` is what the review-threshold calibrator
counts, and it may only *propose* a per-person review threshold change for a coordinator to
approve -- see ADR 0008 (`docs/adr/0008-coordinator-calibrated-review-threshold.md`).

MeResponse.title: MeResponse
MeResponse.description: Who is signed in, and what they still have to do before using the app.

MyDay.title: MyDay
MyDay.description:
"Read my day": a short spoken run-through of the senior's own day, for the browser to read
aloud with its built-in speech. `mode`, `source`, `model` and `steps` as on `CatchUp`.

NotificationItem.title: NotificationItem
NotificationItem.description: One notification for the signed-in member, with what the bell needs to show it.

NotificationKind.title: NotificationKind
NotificationKind.description: What a notification tells its one recipient. Closed: the browser words each one itself.

NotificationPage.title: NotificationPage
NotificationPage.description:
Newest first, across all the member's family groups. Pass `next_before` as `before` for the
next page; None at the end. `unread_count` counts every unread notification, not just this
page's.

NotificationReadRequest.title: NotificationReadRequest
NotificationReadRequest.description: Mark some of your notifications read (`notification_ids`), or all of them (`all`).

OutcomeKind.title: OutcomeKind
OutcomeKind.description:
How a person responded to one piece of outreach.

`ACCEPTED` means only "show me more" -- it is consent to continue, not evidence that anything
helped. What actually happened afterwards is `FollowThrough`, recorded separately, and the two
must never be collapsed: a system that treats a tap as success is optimising engagement, which
is the exact failure mode this product exists to avoid.

`DEFERRED` and `NO_RESPONSE` are also deliberately distinct. "Maybe later" is an active reply
from someone who read the message; `NO_RESPONSE` is silence. Filing the first as the second
both overstates how many people ignore Care+ and, before this split, scored an explicit
deferral as harshly as a refusal.

outcome.description: accepted, declined, deferred, no_response, or activity_recovered. `accepted` means the person asked to see more -- report what they actually did via the follow-through route, not here.

reason.description: Optional context, only meaningful alongside `declined`. Always skippable; never required to submit a response.

OverrideReason.title: OverrideReason
OverrideReason.description:
Why a coordinator did not do what Care+ suggested.

A closed vocabulary rather than free text, because the point of recording it is to be able to
count it: "the system keeps flagging people whose trackers are unreliable" is a finding, and
fifty distinct sentences saying that are not. The optional note beside it carries the detail
and stays on the review row -- it never reaches the operator-readable audit trail, which
records only that a note exists.

PolicyGate.title: PolicyGate
PolicyGate.description:
Which rung of `policy.decide`'s ladder produced the decision.

A report, never an interpretation. The ladder returns at the first guard clause that matches,
and this names that clause -- so `SUPPRESS` appears under two gates (the weekly contact cap
and the accepted-outreach cooldown, which share a rung, a decision and a support priority) and
`NO_ACTION` under six. Without it, every consumer wanting to caption a decision had to
reconstruct the ladder from `PersonState` and drifted: the evaluator surface captioned a
cooldown suppression as "Weekly contact cap reached", which is factually wrong for the person
who was left alone precisely because they had just taken a suggestion up.

Adding this changed no decision. `decide` returns exactly what it returned before, with one
more field describing the return it already made.

PriorOutreach.title: PriorOutreach
PriorOutreach.description:
One thing Care+ already did about this concern, before it asked for a human.

The case card could not answer "what have you tried?" at all: the day-one nudge and day-two
suggestion lived on a separate per-person card that defaulted to one persona regardless of
whose case was on screen, so a coordinator read "activity is 56% below across 4 days" with no
idea whether anything had been offered or whether the person had replied.

`outcome` and `follow_through` are the same enums the outreach history uses, and `None` means
"nothing recorded" -- never "no" and never "ignored". A tap is not success and silence is not
refusal; both distinctions are already load-bearing elsewhere and must not be flattened here.

tables_without_rls.title: Tables Without Rls
tables_without_rls.description: Public ORM tables whose PostgreSQL row-level security is off. The browser never reaches these tables directly -- `anon` and `authenticated` are denied by policy -- and a table with RLS disabled has lost that denial, so any name here makes `status` `not_ready`. Always empty off PostgreSQL: SQLite has no such flag to report on, and no Data API to be exposed to.

ReviewThresholdNotice.title: ReviewThresholdNotice
ReviewThresholdNotice.description: What the senior is told, in fixed wording, after their review threshold changed.

ReviewThresholdNoticeKind.title: ReviewThresholdNoticeKind
ReviewThresholdNoticeKind.description:
Which way the senior-facing notice points: Care+ now waits a little `LATER`, or lets
the care team know a little `SOONER` again.

ServerErrorBody.title: ServerErrorBody
ServerErrorBody.description:
The body of every classified 500. `detail` repeats `message` for clients that read
`detail`, the FastAPI convention the rest of the API follows. Plain language only: no field
path, stored value or framework text.

ServerErrorCode.title: ServerErrorCode
ServerErrorCode.description: How a server-side failure is classified (`error_responses.py`).

SpeechRequest.title: SpeechRequest
SpeechRequest.description:
One sentence of a "Read my day" script to be spoken by the Kokoro voice. Never stored, never
logged; only a hash of it keys the in-memory audio cache.

SpeechVoice.title: SpeechVoice
SpeechVoice.description:
Whether "Read my day" can use the Kokoro voice here, the default voice and its name, and the
other Kokoro voices on offer. When not available, the browser reads with its own voice.

SpeechVoiceOption.title: SpeechVoiceOption
SpeechVoiceOption.description: One Kokoro voice the listener may choose, and its name on the card.

StatedContextExplanation.title: StatedContextExplanation
StatedContextExplanation.description:
The person's own account of a quiet stretch, while it is still in force.

Exposed as structured fields rather than left implicit in `rationale` because the web's
Decision Audit panel captions the `stated_explanation` gate (`decided_by_gate`) from these
fields, and is explicitly forbidden from string-matching the free-text rationale to do it (see
`apps/web/lib/view-models.ts`).

`explains_through` is a *simulated* day, like `stated_on` -- see `context_explanation.py` for
why a wall-clock window would never expire in a demo.

TaskRequest.title: TaskRequest
TaskRequest.description:
A new or changed task. A repeating one is stored once and happens on every day it repeats,
until `repeat_until` (inclusive) or forever.

TaskTick.title: TaskTick
TaskTick.description: One day of a task ticked done.

WearableStatus.title: WearableStatus
WearableStatus.description:
Whether the senior's watch is connected, when it last synced, and its battery. Simulated
until a real device adapter exists (`source` says so); never a health signal.
